titleEn: When the Owl Hoots, Time for Sleep!

pages.text: Hoot, hoot. An owl called from the mountain. Wearing a vermilion scarf, Yuki stacked wooden pieces beside the brazier. "Just one more layer!"
Grandma warmed her hands in gray layered clothes. "When the owl calls, it's bedtime." "I'm not sleepy! I'll stack to the roof!" Yuki shook their head and hugged an armful of wood.
But their eyelids grew heavy. Wooden pieces rolled off their knees. Their mouth opened in a yawn. "Oh? My eyes keep closing..."
Grandma gently covered the brazier with ashes, using a long stick. The red fire shrank. The room grew dim, and the owl called again. Hoot.
There were things to do when the owl called. First, spread the quilt! Yuki opened it with both hands. Brown dog Momo lay beside it.
Second, get under the quilt! Yuki pulled it up to their neck. Grandma rested a hand on their forehead and hummed softly, "When the Owl Hoots, Time for Sleep!"
Third, Grandma blew out the lamp. Even in darkness, a rosy glow remained beneath the ashes. "When the Owl Hoots, Time for Sleep!" Grandma's voice was low and warm as brazier ashes.
Now Yuki's turn. Yuki sang softly to Momo, "Time for sleep." Momo tapped the floor with their tail and closed their eyes.
The next evening, at the owl's call, Yuki untied and neatly folded the scarf. "One, stop playing when the owl hoots! Two, under the quilt! Three, sleep when Grandma puts out the lamp!"
In the morning, Grandma kissed Yuki's forehead. An early bedtime made their body light as feathers in the morning. Yuki stretched toward the open door. "When the Owl Hoots, Time for Sleep!"
